1.1: Concerning what befell them at the hand of Meqabis among the Jews in Mesopotamia of Syria; and he slew them utterly, unto the border of Jerusalem, from Jabbok and from Ṭəfʿa, unto the holy precinct.
1.2: For they rose up from Samaria, even unto the border of Jerusalem and all its environs, and slew with the edge of the sword, until none remained except the transgressors. For there joined the Edomites, and the Tyrians, and the Amalekites, with Moab — Meqabis, who destroyed the city of Jerusalem.
1.3: And when the children of Israel sinned, He sent against them the Moabite, Meqabis, and he slew them, all of them, with the sword.
1.4: And because of this the anger of the Lord was kindled against His holy city, and they mustered in their camp.
1.5: And the Edomites and the Elofəli rose up, and seized and took vengeance upon the city of God; for by night He sent them, because they had despised the word of the Lord.
1.6: And as for Meqabis — his city was Remat of Moab — and he rose up with strength from his city, and mustered with those who were with him.
1.7: And they saw all the hosts of Mesopotamia unto Syria, [come] to destroy the city of God. And from there he sought the Elofəlians and the Amalekites, and gave them much silver and gold, and horses and chariots, that they might be with him in the camp.
1.8: And they came in force, and besieged the city, and shed blood like water — the blood of those who dwelt within her.
1.9: And he made Jerusalem like a miller's trough, and made within her filth and dung and every thing displeasing to God — a deed of affliction — and defiled the city of God, which was full of righteousness and holiness.
1.10: And they made the corpses of Thy servants food for the birds of heaven, and the flesh of Thy saints unto the beasts of the desert.
1.11: And they mocked the meek, O ye children of death; and they ripped forth what was in the womb, until God — who trieth the heart and the reins — shall have mercy [and intervene]. For they that have no fear of God did according as Satan taught them.
1.12: And they returned into their tents, rejoicing over the evil they had done unto the people of God; and He took away the shelter and the refuge which I had chosen, from the holy city.
1.13: And when they entered and came into their dwellings, they kept Passover and faḥəl and encamped.

2.1: And thus saith the prophet, the seer, who saith unto him: Now rejoice, O sinner, in the hour of light; but now the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, will avenge Himself upon thee, because shame never touched thy face.
2.2: Our couriers and my horses are worn out, and therefore I have fled to Bedir.
2.3: And I — through thee — from ʾänəsərət they run who pursue thee, and thou shalt not escape from them, nor from the stroke of the Lord which is upon thee.
2.4: And they said unto us: "Gird on the sword; and the drawing of the bow shall not hold me back, nor the därəb of my kwəyan; and I will ʾäkəkoki thee; likewise with the därəb of the sword which shall not avenge thee," saith the Lord, the Holy One of Israel. But there shall come a sore disease into thy heart, which is worse than the drawing of the bow, and than the därəb of kwənat, and than the stroke of siḥ — and it shall not ʾäbäq.
2.5: And a sore disease shall come into thy heart, and thou shalt miss him who would help thee, and he shall not be found; for I will lay my stroke upon thee, and thou shalt not escape from my hand, until I destroy thy remembrance from the earth.
2.6: And He said unto me: I am the Lord thy Creator. When I do this thing swiftly, like the twinkling of an eye — for thou hast girded thy loins and lifted up thy head against My city — for thou art like stubble before the wind, which the fire devoureth before Mine eyes, and like dust which the winds take up and scatter from the face of the earth; so art thou in My hand.
2.7: For I will lay my stroke upon thee, and thy Creator shall have no mercy upon thee; and I will not spare anything that is in thee, and none shall remain that hideth itself in all thy mountains.
2.8: And now repent from all the evil which thou hast done; and if thou hast repented and humbled thyself before the Lord with sighing and weeping, and hast asked of Him with a pure heart — the Lord will forgive thy sin in all wherein thou hast sinned before Him.
2.9: And at that time Meqabis wept before the Lord because of his sin, and clothed himself with dust; for the Lord had mercy upon him.
2.10: And I understood that God will not tarry the evil which He spoke by the mouth of His prophet; for His eyes are watchful and do not sleep, and His ears are open and are not deaf. And I heard the word which He spoke, and He will do it at once, like the twinkling of an eye.
2.11: And he tore off his garment, and put on rough sackcloth, and cast dust upon his head, and wept, and cried aloud before the Lord his God, because of the evil which he had done.

3.1: And the prophet spoke, for Remat of Moab was near unto Syria.
3.2: And he tore at the ground, and came even unto his loins, and wept with bitter weeping, and repented because of the sin which he had done before the Lord.
3.3: And thus said the Lord unto the prophet: Go to the land of Judah; enter; go to the land of Remat, unto Meqabis the prince of Moab, and say unto him: Thus saith the Lord: For it was not of thine own hand that thou didst this — that thou shouldest devour by the strength of My might and by My təʿyənət  — thou hast destroyed the holy city; but I am the Lord; My messenger is with thee; of Myself, by My will, I sent thee, that thou shouldest destroy My city.
3.4: For from My ʿəʿat  with all səsəʿət  and fornication and deceit.
3.5: And I took hold and preserved thee alive, and set thee in thy place; and not by thyself — wherein thou girdedst thy loins — and thou saidst: "I will rodək  it, the city, by the strength of my hand." And now, because of thy children whom thou hast begotten, the Lord will forgive thy sin.
3.6: And now repent with all thy heart, and be steadfast, and be not negligent; for the negligent do not attain unto repentance.
3.7: And blessed are those who repent with all their heart, and do not return unto affliction and sin, in all their repentance for their evil.
3.8: And they attain with weeping and sighing, and with much prayer, and with worship unto the Lord who zäfä ṭäromu ; for He saith unto the penitents: Ye — after ye have erred and have repented — ʾəliʿayä , ye.
3.9: And to the proud He saith: After he hath sinned, when he cometh unto Him in repentance, because of thy contrition and because of thy fear, He will forgive thy sin. For I am the Lord, a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and unto the fourth generation; but unto them that love Me and keep My commandments I do mercy with them, unto a thousand generations.
3.10: And now, because of these thy children whom thou hast begotten, keep My covenant which is with thee; and I have accepted the repentance which I have wrought, because of the evil of thy deeds, saith the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, who kəluyəmäləkə .
3.11: And at that time he went out from gəb , and worshipped the prophet, saying: "Such and such — may the Lord grant me to inherit, that I be not cut off from thee; but grant me what thou wilt. For I have despised God, and have not walked in His commandment, as my fathers [did not]; for we have no law. And moreover thou knowest that we serve idols, as our fathers taught us."
3.12: And I — I have not heard the word of His prophets of God until now; for I have sinned, who have walked in my sin, and in the pride of my heart, and in the girding of my loins, wherein I despised the commandment of God; and I have not walked in His commandment, nor kept that which He commanded me.
3.13: And the prophet took up [his word] and said unto him: I have understood that now thy repentance is accepted; for there is none among you of your kindred who any longer trusteth in his sin.
3.14: And from henceforth forsake the worship of idols, and return thou into the counsel of God, that thy repentance may be in truth. And he worshipped at the prophet's feet; and the prophet raised him up, and commanded him all that is fitting — good deeds.
3.15: And he did according as God commanded him, and entered into his house.
3.16: And Meqabis set himself aright, and removed from his house all sägäl , and idols, and marəyan , and məṭəʿawəyan , and mäsägəlan .
3.17: And the children of Ṣewan, whom he had brought from Jerusalem — he examined them śärkä , and declared unto them all the commandment of God, and His law, and His ordinance, according as their fathers had done them.
3.18: And he set over his house wise men, from the children of Ṣewa.
3.19: And moreover, from the young among their wise men he appointed [teachers] [supplied] — those who keep — that they might teach them the way of God, according as the children of Israel did His law and His ordinance and His statutes, and all their abominations which the Moabites yətəḥeräm  — let him hear from the children of Ṣewa.
3.20: And he shattered their abominations, and all their sägälat , and all their idols, and all their mäwaṣəḥt , and their məśəwaʿ , from their səbuḥ , from the ḥäragit  of his märaʿəy , and from the mäqwəʿal  of ṭäli , which he sacrifices to his gods — śärkä ; and he declared.
3.21: And he sacrificeth unto them, and worshippeth them in every deed, continually; and he asketh of them, and believeth in them, and doeth their will in all that the ministers of his gods tell him.
3.22: And he turned not aside from their words in all that they told him; for it pleased him in all that they had done for him.
3.23: But as for Meqabis, who was among them — he forsook the way.
3.24: And when the seer heard the word which the prophet had spoken unto him, he set his way straight into repentance; and all his household set straight their way, [learning] from the children of Israel, at that time. For the children of Israel — at one time they show mercy unto him, and at another they chastise him; they teach him, and turn him unto the Lord.
3.25: And when He saw that they were humbled under the hands of those that oppressed them, and they cried out before Him — then the Prince teacheth them, remembering the covenant of their fathers, when they cry unto Him, for the sake of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, their fathers.
3.26: And after He had saved them, they forgot Him who had saved them, and returned unto the worship of idols.
3.27: And the Prince sendeth against them peoples that oppress them; and when they oppress them and afflict them, they cry out unto the Lord. And at that time He teacheth them, and forgiveth them; for He loveth them, for they are the work of His hands.
3.28: And again, when He giveth them rest, they return to seek favor from it, with the worship of the idols which ʿawədomu ; and the work of their hands was evil.
3.29: And He raiseth up against them the peoples of Elofəli, and Moab, and Midian, and Syria, and Egypt; and they weep and cry out when their məʿw  oppresseth them, and he afflicteth them, and subdueth them, and taketh possession of them. And He raiseth up for them judges, that the judges might save them.

4.1: And there was [one] who believed: Hosea.
4.2: And there was [one] who believed: Gideon.
4.3: And there was [one] who believed: Samson, and Barak, and Deborah, and Judith — whether among women, whether among the humble — He raiseth up for them judges, that they might save them from those that oppress them, and that He might save them from the hand of all their oppressors.
4.4: And according as He willed, the Lord saved them from those that oppressed them.
4.5: And they rejoiced greatly in all that He set straight for them: in the sowing of their land, and He multiplied their cattle, and in all pasture that is in the field and in the desert.
4.6: And He blesseth for them their cattle, and their plantings, and all that they hold, whether of the house or of the desert; He blesseth for them, and their cattle do not miscarry, for with His eyes He watcheth over them, and He loveth them exceedingly, for they are a generation of the righteous.
4.7: And when they became evil in their deeds, He cast them into the hand of their oppressors.
4.8: And when the Prince slayeth them, they bethink themselves, and return, and cry out unto the Lord God their Creator.
4.9: And when they return with all their heart, He forgiveth them, and their former iniquity He remembereth not unto them; for He remembereth that they are flesh and blood, and in them is the anointing of the conscience of this world, and devils.
4.10: And Meqabis, when he heard this word which God ordained on the mount of His sanctuary, contended in repentance.
4.11: And he turned not aside from doing what he had seen; and he heard this word. And because of all the ḫirut which the children of Israel yəgä bəru — for God forgave them; and when God chastiseth them, if they keep the commandment, they weep and cry out, and again He forgiveth them, and they do His commandment.
4.12: And likewise Meqabis made straight his way, and kept His commandment, and walked in the commandment of the Lord God of Israel.
4.13: The Prince, when he heard, and in all that the children of Israel counsel — likewise let him counsel with the keeper of His commandment, unto the Lord.
4.14: And he established his house and his children, that they might walk in all his way and in His commandments, unto the Lord.
4.15: And the ḥərmät of the Jews which they keep — he too shall keep; and the commandments which the Jews keep, when he heareth, likewise he shall do; and the mäbaləʿt which the Jews keep he shall keep, though he be of another people — a Moabite.
4.16: And the tithe he shall tithe; and the firstborn of his cattle, and of his flock, and of his ʿədug, and all that is clean he shall give; and the sacrifices which the Jews sacrifice, likewise he shall sacrifice, facing the way toward Jerusalem.
4.17: And [the offering] for firstfruits, and [the offering] for sin, and the freewill [offering], and the sacrifice of salvation, and the sacrifice of zäləf.
4.18: And the first of the fruits, and the moṣaḥt which the Jews bring forth — likewise he shall bring forth, and give unto the Levite whom he hath appointed; and all that the Jews do, likewise he shall do. And the lifting of incense.
4.19: And he made märanat and milonat and ṭäräṗezat and däbatərat and baḥrəyat and ḥoṣadat, and kə bəʿa wəguʿä for the holy maḥətot and mänəṭolaʿt, as they do within the holy of holies of Israel, when they keep the feast unto the Lord.
4.20: For they walked in His law and in His ordinance; and if God had not kept them alive, He would not have given them into the hand of their oppressors. Thus did Meqabis in all his way.
4.21: And he prayeth at all times unto the Lord God of Israel, that they may be led, and that he may not separate from the congregation of Israel who have chosen and done [His] will.
4.22: And again he prayeth that He may give seed in Zion, and ʾäbəyat in Jerusalem; and that He may save them from those which He spoke by the mouth of the prophet; and that his repentance may be accepted in all wherein he hath repented.
4.23: And he wept before the Lord with sighing, [praying] that He would not destroy his seed from the earth, and that He would keep him in his coming in and his going out.
4.24: And of the peoples of Moab who were under his hand, unto Meqabis they gave heed, that they might believe; for in the right way walk their angels, and they keep judgment, and do [His] will; and they establish judgment in their lands, and their districts are at peace, and they see that he is upright and exceedingly wise, Meqabis.
4.25: And they come unto him, and hear the judgment of his righteousness, and his ḫirut  — unto Meqabis.
4.26: And in it are many ṭərit, and ʾägəbərət, and ʾäʿəmat, and ʾäʿədug, and camels; and in it are horses that wear the sword.
4.27: And after this he worshippeth the Lord; when he walketh in ṣäbəʿ, there is none that moʿo except by night that moʿa.
4.28: But they come with the strength of their gods, that they may ṣäbəʿ him and curse him in the name of their gods; and there is none that yəmäwəʿ him, for he hath founded his trust upon the Lord his God.
4.29: And it came to pass, while he did thus, and while he yəmäwəʿ the oppressor, that he brought the peoples under his hand.
4.30: And he avengeth the oppressed, and justifieth the judgment of the children of death.
4.31: And he receiveth the meek and the children of death in their affliction; and he satisfieth the hungry with his food, and clotheth the naked with his garment.
4.32: And he rejoiceth in his conduct and in the work of his hands; and he giveth of that which he hath, unstintingly; and the tithe he giveth unto the house of God. And while Meqabis did this, he rested well.

5.1: And he forsook his ʿəgwäl ; and the young children grew, according as their father had ordained for them, and kept the ordinance of their house; and all that was among them they observed, and they cried not nädäy  — O ye children of death, and ye meek.
5.2: And they feared the Lord, and gave their goods to the poor, and were entreated in all wherein their father had entreated them; and they comfort the meek and the children of death in their affliction, and are to them father and mother, and bear them from the hand of their oppressors, and comfort them in all that befell them — trouble and sorrow.
5.3: And they continued, while thus they did.
5.4: And after him came Ṣiruṣaydan, king of the Chaldeans, and he destroyed all their cities, and stirred them up against the children of Meqabis, and destroyed all their districts.
5.5: And he maḫräk  all their goods, and kiyahomuni ; he seized them and carried them off into his districts — the mäməlakəya  of idols — who walk not in His commandment nor in His statutes of God, but in all evil and fornication and defilement and səsəʿət  and ṣərəfät ; and they remembered not their God.
5.6: And they devoured all carrion and blood, and the food of wild beasts, and bətək , and everything displeasing to God — [the Ge'ez has a negation here, ʾiyəbäləʿu "they did not devour", which contradicts the vice-catalogue context and is probably corrupt,?] — and they have no law from any of the righteous commandments which are written in the Orit.
5.7: And they knew not the Lord, that He is their Creator and their Savior, who brought them out from their mother's womb, and nourished them as is fitting.
5.8: And they have no law in judgment, who walk in affliction and təʿgələt  and zəmut  and defilement, while they take their father's wife, and their mother's sister; and they do all evil, and take their sisters and their kinswomen; and they have no law.
5.9: And all their ways are gloom and darkness and defilement and zəmut .
5.10: But as for the children of Meqabis — they keep, in all that is among them, the təḫrəmət ; and they eat not carrion nor bətək , nor any of their defilement and their sin, [abstaining] from the children of the Chaldeans. For evil and many are their deeds which are not written in this book, which the children of the ʾÄräbamayan  do — sinners, and the rebellious, hypocrites, and the deceitful, and deceitful ṣiʿ, and defilement, and təʿəgələt.
5.11: And there is nothing upon them that pleaseth God their Creator.
5.12: And again they worship idols whose name is Beelphegor; and they worship him and believe in him as God their Creator. For he is deaf and dumb, and seeth not nor heareth; for a graven image is he, the work of men's hands, which they have säbäk  — nähäbe  silver and gold — the work of the children of ʾəmäḥəyaw , that hath no knowledge nor breath.
5.13: And he eateth not, and he drinketh not.
5.14: And he killeth not, and he maketh not alive.
5.15: And he planteth not, and he plucketh not up.
5.16: He yäḥäsəm not, and he yaśeni not.
5.17: He yanäṣ not, and he yabəʿl not.
5.18: He rebuketh not, and he forgiveth not; but baḥətu  — ʿəqəfət shall be — for the destruction of the ʿabədan  of the Chaldean people.

6.1: And the proud Ṣiruṣaydan appointed — to the anger of the Lord — lying priests and ministers of idols.
6.2: And they sacrifice unto them, and bring [offerings] forth unto them.
6.3: And it seemeth to him that they eat and drink.
6.4: And he giveth them, unto those who ṣäbəḥ , flocks and cattle and ḥäragit  and ʾäṭäli ; and they sacrifice śärkä , and he declareth; and he eateth of that defiled sacrifice.
6.5: And not of their own will did they do this unto him; but läʾäbəʾəni  they were given and made, that they might eat [of the sacrifices] unto their gods.
6.6: And when he saw the children of Meqabis, that they are righteous and worship the Lord their Creator, he desired them; [and] the ministers of the idols yasəḥət them, that they might eat of the sacrifices and eat from that defiled sacrifice. But these blessed ones refused them.
6.7: And he asked them why they refused; for they keep their father's commandment, and are steadfast in good deeds, and fear the Lord exceedingly.
6.8: And when he was wroth against them, and was stern against them, and afflicted them.
6.9: And they told Ṣiruṣaydan the king that he refuseth to worship and to sacrifice unto his gods.
6.10: And because of this the king was moved with pity, and grieved, and commanded that they bring them; and they brought them, and he set them before him, and said unto them: "Eat ye, and worship ye my gods."
6.11: And they took up [their word] and said unto him: "As for us, we will not obey thee in this matter, and we will not sacrifice unto thy defiled gods."
6.12: And he threatened them with many tortures, and prevailed not against them; for their hearts were steadfast unto the Lord.
6.13: And he kindled the fire, and cast them in; and they delivered up their souls unto the Lord.
6.14: And He showed him their life after their death — while they held their swords, məlu ḥätä  — while he slept upon his royal bed by night; and great fear [came upon him].
6.15: And he said unto them: "What shall I do for you? My ʾägaʿəzt  — bəqwəʿuni  — and I will not lift it for myself, that I may do all that ye commanded me; and I will fear Him exceedingly."
6.16: And they told him all that is fitting, saying: "Remember that the Lord thy Creator is He; and there is One who shall shatter thee from this thy pride, and bring thee down into Gehenna below, with Diabolos thy father. And there thou shalt fulfill all thy judgment, according as thou burnedst us with fire — while there was none that had sinned against thee — and while we worship the Lord our Creator, and worship Him in fear of the Lord."
6.17: For He is the Creator of all, who made heaven and earth and sea, and all that is in them.
6.18: The sun and the moon and the stars, and all creatures which God created lälihu .
6.19: And there is no other god besides Him, in heaven above nor in earth beneath, who is able for all; and there is none like unto Him, who killeth and maketh alive, who rebuketh and forgiveth.
6.20: And there is none that escapeth from His hand; for He is the mälak  of heaven and earth.
6.21: And there is none that transgresseth His commandment [who escapeth?] from Him who created him, save thou and thy məʿlay  and those like thee — mäməʿləyan  who have blinded their hearts — they, and Satan thy father; and thou and thy gods shall go down together into Gehenna, whence there is no escape, for ever.
6.22: For it was not thou by thyself who didst this, but Satan thy teacher, who taught thee this evil deed, that thou mightest be put to shame before us.
6.23: And thou hast not known the Lord thy Creator, and thou hast lifted up thy head as [though thou wert] the Lord thy Creator.
6.24: And thou hast boasted in the work of thy hands and in thy idols, until God humble thee, and bring thee down to the mäfəḥt  of Gehenna; and He will avenge Himself upon thee for all the iniquity and sin which thou hast done upon the earth.

7.1: "Woe unto thee, thou, and those like thee, who have not known Him — the Lord who created you — and have not known His commandment and His word; for ye shall be cut off, whence no repentance availeth, when ye are punished in the straits of Sheol."
7.2: "And ye shall have no escape from it for ever — thou and thy gods, and those who sacrifice and worship unto them as [if they were] God your Creator — unto those which have neither soul nor breath, and which avenge not them that ʾäḥsämä  them, and show no mercy to them that ʾäśänäyä  them."
7.3: "For the work of man's hand are they, in whom Satan speaketh, to destroy the heart of fools like thee, O fool! — that he may bring down you and the ministers of your gods, and those demons that command you, into Gehenna of fire."
7.4: "For ye have not known that none profiteth you; ye err and are destroyed."
7.5: "And better than you shall be the beasts which God created for your food — and the oxen witəni  and the dogs käläbatəni  — for they have no judgment again, save one death."
7.6: "But as for you, ye shall die, and be judged again in the terror of Gehenna, whence there is no escape for ever."
7.7: And when they had said this, they departed and were hidden from him.
7.8: And Ṣiruṣaydan was in great fear and trembling, and it left him not until morning.
7.9: And then he went to where he had cast the bodies of the righteous, and found them not; for he desired to yəqä  with them and səʿän  them. For God had hidden them, that he should not təḫaśəś  from their flesh.

8.1: And he went in pride and in təməyənət  of heart.
8.2: For the sun stood in the midst of heaven until he destroyed the armies of the Canaanites and the Hivites and the Hittites and the Perizzites and the Jebusites; and he slew them, and bound their feet in their fetters, and slew them with the edge of the sword, and wəsät  in the bäʿat , and heaped stones upon them.
8.3: And he went about in all ʿəbäd  and evil and hukät .
8.4: And what we told before them: he ploweth and he nagwʿ  and he eateth.
8.5: The kings in one bäʿat  — and by his prayer he made the sun stand at Gibeon, that he might destroy their armies; and he slew in one moment.
8.6: And he knew not God, that He is his Creator — who saith: "My time is become as the time of heaven."
8.7: And he thought in his heart that from him the sun riseth.
8.8: And he rose up bägod  and encamped in the land of Zebulon, and took ṣ́äbʿa  and Macedonia, and took provisions from Samaria, and gave it to ʾäsäbäʾəməsorəya .
8.9: And he yäḫdr  unto the däwäl  of Kedar, and extended unto Sidon, and did  gəbər in Achaia, and raised  kəśad  unto the Sea of Tekeze, and yətmäyṭ , and sent his messengers unto the Indian Sea.
8.10: And thus he raiseth kəśad  unto heaven.
8.11: And his head is not ʾätəḥt  but [he is] in all evil and təzəḫrət .
8.12: And all his ways are in däḥṣ́  and darkness and pride and ʿələwät  and qəṭəqaṭe  and kəʿiw  of blood.
8.13: And all his fəmot  which God hateth, he doeth — according as Säbəlanəyos taught him, mämə həru  for evil and təʿgələt  and ṣug ; and he yagʿər  the children of death, and pitieth not nädäy .
8.14: And the kings of the nations he brought under his hand, and slew them.
8.15: And the angels of the enemies he judged; and many nations he ʾägrär , and did with them as he willed.
8.16: And he spared not, and there was none that escaped, from the Sea of Tarshish unto the Sea of ʾIyariko .
8.17: And he worshippeth idols, and eateth dead things and blood and bətk , and sacrificeth unto the gods; and in his heart there is no justice, but in all his ways there is nothing save fətəḥ  and mäʿat  and qwəṭʿa  and häkäk . For he became a mädänəgṣ  unto the nations under his hand, and did with them as he willed.
8.18: And there is no fear of God before their eyes; for all that he ʾädämo * yəgä bərə  before him, and he walketh in təməyənət  before God his Creator.*
8.19: And he regardeth Him not, that his God, even the Lord, will requite him according as he did evil against his neighbour, when the day shall seize him with his mäʿat .
8.20: And He will avenge Himself in His time, according as He śäräw  the former sinners; for He saith: "I am the Lord, who avenge Me upon the proud, who walk not in My commandment; and I will root out their memorial from the earth."
8.21: And the wicked shall be requited according as they did evil.
8.22: But as for the doers of good, goodness shall be given unto them from the Lord.
8.23: And according as He ʾiyas  destroyed the kings of Canaan in one day, unto
8.24: Thus shall He find those who despise God by their evil deeds.

9.1: And thou, O man — and God is not [with thee?] — why dost thou exalt thyself, thou who today art a man, and tomorrow shalt be earth and ashes, and shalt become wood and boards in thy grave?
9.2: And the [depths?] of Sheol shall be given unto thee, and unto those who do thy works; for thy teacher Säbəlyanos hath revealed, who brought upon his head the sin of all the world, because he caused our father Adam to err through his pride.
9.3: For he who refused to bow down to the work of his God, in the pride of his head and in the loftiness of his kəśad .
9.4: And thou, like thy teacher, hast refused to bow to the Lord thy God.
9.6: And vengeance was taken upon them, and they went down into Sheol, because of the evil of their deeds which they did upon the earth.
9.7: And thou, like them, shalt go down into Gehenna.
9.8: Thou imaginest to snatch from His hand — from God! — for mäʿato  and häk  and tähäk : the worship of God, which gave thee dominion over [all?].
9.9: And He proved thee, whether thou wouldest do His will or not; and if thou hast made straight thy way upon the earth, God shall prosper thy paths, and all that thy hand hath gotten He shall prosper, and shall bless thee; and all thine adversaries and thine enemies He shall destroy for thee.
9.10: And thou shalt rejoice in thy ṣ́aʿat  and in thy bäʿat , and in the fruit of thy belly, and in thy storehouses, and in thy pastures; and whithersoever thou puttest forth thy fingers, and all that He hath put in thy heart shall be commanded unto thee — for from God it was commanded unto thee. Thus shalt thou do, and build, and plant, and tənəśət **
9.11: But if thou hast refused to hear His word and His law of God, and hast not walked in His judgment, thou hast nowhere to snatch from His hand — from God! — like all the rebellious who were before thee, who worshipped not God in purity, and trusted not in His righteous judgment; for righteousness is all His judgment.
9.12: And there is none that hideth himself from before His eyes; and all is naked and manifest before Him.
9.13: Now His is the dominion of kings, and He is the overturner of the thrones of the mighty.
9.14: And He is the exalter of the humble, and the raiser of the fallen.
9.15: And He is the looser of the prisoners, and the raiser of the dead; and those whose flesh is worn out and become as dust, He shall awaken them at the time He willeth — for He is an overshadowing of mercy from Him.
9.16: But those who did evil, He shall raise them — a däyən  resurrection — for they despised [God], and He shall requite them.
9.17: And upon the earth He shall yamasən  their seed; for the rebellious are they, against the law and the ordinance of the Lord God.
9.18: And let not sinners plot in their counsel against the righteous; for strait is their path for the righteous, [far] from the ways of sinners.
9.19: And as heaven is high above the earth, so far are the ways of the righteous from the ways of sinners.
9.20: But as for the ways of sinners: the doing of ṣug  and təʿəgələt  and iniquity and fornication and deceit and səsəʿət ; and going after strange property, and drunkenness in iniquity.
9.21: And räwiṣ  in the käʿəwät  of blood, and ʾamasən  in that which is unclean; and səʾanəbəʿa  the children of death; and eating carrion and blood, and eating the flesh of ḥarawəyan ; and the camel and the ḥawir  in a woman ḥaräsä , and təkət  which is not cleansed.
9.22: And all these are the deeds of sinners: broad is the way, and wide is the net of Satan, which leadeth into ḫaʾgʷäl  and into eternal judgment.
9.23: But as for the ways of the righteous: narrow and mäqəʿan , which lead unto life — humility, and yähawət , love and peace, fasting and prayer, and purity of flesh, and abstinence from unclean foods: carrion and bətk  and fornication, and ḥawir
9.24: And they abstain from every foul deed, and from foul foods which are not [permitted?] in the law, and from foul deeds which God loveth not — for all these do the sinners.
9.25: But the righteous are set apart from all evil ways, which God loveth not.
9.26: And He loveth them, and hath mercy upon them, and shall deliver them from all their tribulations.
9.27: But as for sinners, Satan shall qänəy  them; for they have transgressed His law and His ordinance, and [all] that He loveth.

10.1: And ye, O kings and rulers, walk not in his ways, but fear ye the Lord God, who created you and hath kept you until now.
10.3: For Balak, son of Zippor, when the children of Israel came by the way of Amalek, to inherit the land of the Canaanites and the Hittites and the Perizzites.
10.4: And he said to Balaam: "Curse thou them for me; for whom thou cursest is cursed, and whom thou blessest is blessed. And I will give thee much gold and silver, which shall honour thee, that thou curse them for me."
10.5: And Balaam came, while he looked for his iniquity; and Balak son of Zippor showed him where the children of Israel were encamped
10.6: And he performed divination, and offered sacrifices, and slew bulls and rams, from their səbuḥ ; and he desired to curse the children of Israel.
10.7: But God willed not that he should curse them; but He turned the curse into blessing, by His own word.
10.8: And He said: "Those who bless thee shall be blessed, and those who curse thee shall be cursed; for thou art the people of God, whom He hath chosen; and thou art the dwelling of the Beloved who cometh from on high."
10.9: Then Balak son of Zippor was grieved and angry and enraged, when he [Balaam] blessed them before him, though he had commanded him to curse them.
10.10: And Balaam said unto him: "I will not curse those whom God hath blessed; for the people whom God hath chosen is come into this land."
10.11: And Balak son of Zippor said to Balaam: "I desired that thou shouldest curse them for me, but thou hast not cursed them; but blessing, thou hast blessed them exceedingly before me. And I — the fullness of my house, gold and silver, would I have given thee, if thou hadst said 'Give me,' and hadst cursed them for me. But thou, blessing, hast blessed them, and hast done me no good; and I will do thee no good."
10.12: And Balaam said: "I cannot transgress nor alter the word of God; but what God hath set as a word in my mouth, that will I speak."
10.13: And I will not stake my goods upon my life; for had I coveted my goods, God had mercy upon me, that I should not curse the blessed people.
10.14: For God said to Jacob their father: "Those who bless thee, blessed let them be; and those who curse thee, cursed let them be. For every one that blesseth thee is blessed."
10.15: But he who curseth thee without cause is cursed. Make straight thy deeds and thy ways, that God may love thee.
10.16: And be not like the former people, who despised God by their evil; and He täḥäyäyomu  them — and there are those whom He destroyed by the waters of ʾAyəh [the Flood?].
10.17: And there are those whom He destroyed by the hand of their enemies; and He brought an enemy, an evil people, who took them captive, and led away their kings with their prophets and their Levites.
10.18: And He brought them unto a strange land which they knew not, and scattered them, and maḫarək-ed them, and qäśäf-ed them, and ʾamasän-ed their land.
10.19: And they made Jerusalem a ruin, as a field; for they took the ṭəqom  and qəṣər  from the holy city.
10.20: And the priests were led away, and the law was rent, and they fell into the hands of kwənat .
10.21: And the ʿəberat  were led away, and none wept for their dead that died; for they were carried off, and [it was] upon their heads
10.22: And the children wept, and the ʾäʿərug  were täḫaḏfəru ; and they [the invaders] pitied not the face of the elder nor the aged.
10.23: And not those in the assembly, and not dənagəl  — and they ʾamasänu-ed all that they found within their cities, and ʾafəläs-ed them unto a strange land which they knew not. For when God willed, wrath came upon His people; He yaqädəm-ed the näśət  of His sanctuary.
10.24: And therefore, when God täḥäyäyomu  the children of Israel, God made Jerusalem a ruin; it shall be plowed as a field — for at all times they despise their Creator.
10.25: But He will not destroy them utterly; for He will spare them for the sake of their fathers — and not for their own sake doth He spare them — but because He loveth their fathers: Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, who reigned in righteousness, and ḥoru * dəmeyəhu  in righteousness toward their Creator.*
10.26: And He hath set them in the məkəʿəbit  of glory, both in heaven and on earth.
10.27: And likewise ye, O kings and rulers, who are in this passing world — remember ye those before you, who ḥoru  in purity, that they might inherit the kingdom of heaven; and their name is comely from generation to generation.
10.28: And thou, that thy kingdom may be established and thy name prosper, like those before thee, the good kings, who pleased God by the goodness of their lives.

11.1: From among them — and not their ʾaṣəmət  and not their ʾaləba  — that which is not a brazen censer, which they brought into the house of God by the command of God; for He said: "Their censers are hallowed, by the offering of their bodies."
11.2: And for me, O sinner, grant me forgiveness; for I have done evil before Thee. And for these, śəräy  to them; for Thou art merciful and forgiving.
11.3: And thus He ʾastäśərəyä  to them, to those who ḥämäyəwo .
11.4: And for this, Phinehas was zealous.
11.5: And God loved him exceedingly above all the sons of the Levites his brethren; and he was tämasälo  as God [was] among them; for to the priesthood He appointed them.
11.6: But those who transgressed, the sons of Korah — the earth swallowed them, and brought them down alive into Sheol, in soul and in flesh, with their households and their cattle; and all, every one, according as he spoke, it was done unto him — for he loved the Lord his God, and transgressed not His commandment.
11.7: And likewise thou — if thou transgress not the commandment of God, God will do thy desire for thee, and will love thy word, and will keep thy kingdom.
11.8: And the sons of Korah and Asaph, who transgressed the commandment, against Moses, and murmured against him, because he said unto them: "Make straight your souls unto God."
11.9: And they said unto him: "Are we not sons of Levi, that we should do the work of the priesthood in the chosen tabernacle?"
11.10: And they took their censers to burn incense; and they went and offered incense, but God accepted not their prayer. And by the fire of their censers they were burned and consumed, like wax that melteth in the fire; and none was left
11.11: And therefore God said to Moses and to Aaron: "Gather ye their censers into the tabernacle; and let it be for My house, its gəbərih ; and all that I have appointed for it, from its entrance to its interior."
11.12: And the ʿaśänäy  of its gəbərih  for the holy tabernacle: məsəḥal , ḫoṣadät , kirub , ʾabəḥərt .
11.13: And mäqdəḥ , and mäsawər , and mäwadəd ; and he bound the gädəgädən  for the ṣaḥərat  tabernacle; and mäś waʿət , which they offer in the chosen tabernacle.
11.14: And the freewill sacrifice, and the mädəḫanit  sacrifice, and the bəṣəʿat  sacrifice, and that for sin, and the sacrifice according to the law.
11.15: And all that He commanded Moses in the chosen tabernacle, that they should do — thus He commanded them.
11.16: And let them not provoke jealousy in their God, that His name may be glorified over them, in the tabernacle of His law, of the Lord their God, who ʾasäfəwomu , that He might give them the inheritance of their fathers — a land wherein floweth milk and honey, which He sware unto Abraham.
11.17: And He täkayädä  unto Isaac, and established a covenant unto Jacob.
11.18: And unto Moses and unto Aaron, in the tabernacle, säməʿ .
11.19: And unto Samuel and unto Elias, in Jerusalem, in the tabernacle, in the house of the sanctuary which Solomon built — that it should be the house of God, and the resting-place of His name for the Most High, and the dwelling of the Holy One of Israel.
11.20: For an example and a məstəsəraəy  is this sin, where He showeth to His priests, to those who walk in yəwaḥat .
11.21: And where He heareth the prayer of those who do His will.
11.22: Where He appointeth His law — of the Lord, the Holy One of Israel.
11.23: And where there is made ṣənəḥəḥ  sacrifice, and incense for a sweet savour, unto the Lord, the Holy One of Israel.
11.24: And it is proclaimed upon the height of məsəḥal , in the chosen tabernacle; and He showeth His praise to God, to His chosen, the sons of Jacob, and His holy ones who walk in His commandment; and His judgment is God's.
11.25: But those who yətəʿeyäru  shall be as the sons of Korah, whom the earth swallowed; and likewise the sinners who are like them shall be cast into the judgment of the burning fire, from which there is no escape for ever.

12.1: Woe unto you, mighty men of Israel, who have not kept what I commanded you in the tabernacle, and have not done [His] will — but your own will: pride and təzəḫərt  and fornication and səsəʿət  and drunkenness and drink and mäḥali  in ḥasät .
12.2: And therefore shall My wrath burn upon you, like stubble before the face of fire, and like fire which burneth the mountains, and like a whirlwind which lifteth the ṣäbäl dəkum  from the earth and scattereth it to the height of the air, where no ʿaśər  of it shall be found from its deeds.
12.3: And likewise will I destroy them, all of them that do evil from before My face, saith the Lord, the Holy One of Israel. And remember ye God, who ruleth over all, and there is none who resisteth Him.
12.4: And He loveth them that love Him, and forgiveth them their sins and their evils, for those who walk in His commandment. And be not dənəṣəwan  and dənəzuzan  of heart, in unbelief.
12.5: And make straight your souls unto God, and be like unto Him, that ye may save your souls; and I will save you from the hand of your enemies in the day of your tribulation.
12.6: And when ye are täṣewəʿu-ed, I will say unto you: "Behold, I am with you; and I will save you from the hand of your enemies, and ye shall not be təḥeyäy-ed in the day of your tribulation" — for ye have trusted in Me, and have done My commandment, and have not transgressed My law, and have loved what I love, saith the Lord who ruleth over all.
12.7: And those who love Him, He loveth them; and those who keep His commandment, He hath mercy upon them — for He is merciful and forgiving.
12.8: And great is the mäyəṭ  of His wrath, yet He burneth not with all His mäqəśäfət ; for He is merciful. For He knoweth that they are flesh and blood; and when their souls go forth from their flesh, they enter into their earth.
12.9: And they know not where they were, until when God willed to bring them from where they were not; for He created them from where they were not. And again He took their souls, and brought the earth into its märsət .
12.10: And again He will bring them from where they were not into the being of His will.
12.11: And Ṣiruṣayədan, his ʿaḏlawi  unto God, greatly täʿabəyo  before God; and when he ḫaḏdägo  until the time of His will, he lifted up his head.
12.12: And he said: "Let my days be as the days of heaven; and I am he who maketh the sun to rise, which shall not die for ever."
12.13: And while this word was not yet finished, the angel of death came down, whose name is Ṭələmyakos; and he smote his heart, and he died in that hour. And he was täʾagʷälä  from the beauty of his dwelling, and from the greatness of his pride, and from the evil of his deeds — because he knew not his Creator.
12.14: And the army of the king of the Chaldeans, while they were at the entrance of his city, and təʿəyənt  while they desired his ṣäbiʿot  — and when he died, they went forth and destroyed his city, and mahərəku-ed all his ʾənsas , and left not until he found no rest in ʿarəfət .
12.15: And all his goods they mahərəku-ed, and qwäsaqwəs  they took; and they burned his city with fire, and entered into their own land.

13.2: And they gave their souls to the fire [martyrdom], that they might be saved from the fire of heaven; they knew that this world passeth away.
13.3: And he said unto me: "And no delight dwelleth for zəluf ; for they knew that more grievous is the təʿəyərt  of God than the təʿəyərt of the servants of the living, and more grievous is the wrath of God than the wrath of the king."
13.4: And He reckoneth one day — they shall rejoice in the ʾaʿəṣədat  of Paradise — than a thousand years of life upon earth; and for long days He reckoneth one hour. Forgive  ziʾakä , O my Lord.
13.5: Their hands [are] good who ḫəburä ; they gave their souls unto death. They knew that təśeniyuḫarit  is their life, rather than this earthly, passing one.
13.6: But Thou, O my Lord, abidest for ever; and Thy years which shall not fail, and Thy memorial from generation to generation.
13.7: And all this, and the like, ḥaläyu  the sons of the Meqabyan; and they ʾabdäru-ed and ʾabdäru-ed, trusting in God, and refused the polluted sacrifice of liḥa .
13.8: And therefore they gave their flesh as wax for God's sake. They knew that the dead shall rise, and they knew that there shall be judgment after the resurrection.
13.9: But those who know not and believe not the resurrection of the dead — they knew
13.10: And He showed them that all passeth away; and they gave their souls unto death, that from God they might find məzəgana  — because they believed in Him, and bowed not to idols, and ate not the sacrifice of the dead and of pollution.
13.11: And therefore they knew that He will make them rejoice in the latter day, in soul and in flesh. For while they were with wife and children, they knew not the taste of this world, nor the bitterness of death; and they gave their souls unto death. They knew that there shall be a resurrection in the latter day, in soul and in flesh.
13.12: And they knew that they shall reign — who kept the ordinances of God — in the world to come, for generation to generation, and for long days, where there is no sickness and no sorrow.
13.13: There, there is no sickness and no sorrow, and no death; and with those who believed in the word of God — the chosen kings and rulers — and gave their souls unto death, like wax in the midst of fire, while they beheld with the mind of their heart that which is to come.
13.14: And they shall shine, zäyəbərəh  their faces, sevenfold more than the sun; and that they may rejoice in His love at the resurrection of all, in soul and in flesh.

14.1: As for me, it grieveth me exceedingly, and it yatekəz  me and yəqäləy  my heart, concerning the Judahites and Samaritans and Pharisees and Sadducees, who believe not the resurrection of the dead. The Judahites say: "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die; and thereafter we shall see none."
14.2: And the Samaritans say: "Our flesh shall not rise, for it shall become dust."
14.3: But if there be a resurrection — we believe in the resurrection of our souls; for the soul, when the flesh dieth, dieth not. For it is as the wind, which is not seen, and as the sound of thunder; and none can speak it nor show it.
14.4: But our flesh is seen by all, and becometh ashes and dust; for the beasts devour it, and the ʿəṣeyat  devour it in the grave.
14.5: And as for them that devoured it, they become ashes, and no ʿaśər  of them is found; for they become as grass, and as though they had never been created, they become ashes.
14.6: And by this are found the bodies which bäləyu  And thus say the Pharisees: "We believe in the resurrection of the dead; but He will clothe the souls in the heavens with another flesh than that which was on earth."
14.7: And thus say the Sadducees: "When our soul goeth forth from our flesh, we shall not rise from the dead; and they have no resurrection of the dead — neither for soul nor for flesh. And when we die, we shall not rise."
14.8: And for this they err exceedingly, and it yatikəz  me concerning them; for they speak ṣərəfät  against God and His praise.
14.9: And they have no hope of salvation, for they believed not in God who would justify them; but they have no hope of salvation and of the resurrection of the dead.
14.10: And O blind Judahite, thou hast tasätäʿabəyinu  against God, who brought thee from where thou wast not who sowed thee, He ʿabəqulo  thy soul and thy flesh, in His likeness and in His image.
14.11: And think thou not thus; for thou shalt not escape from His hand. Unto God thou shalt rise, how while thou desirest not; and thou shalt be judged while thou lovest not. For the cord of Sheol is in thy kəśad , which seizeth thee until the day of thy death.
14.12: For in the belly thou shalt təśärəf  for thyself; from the gunəd  of Sheol is this cord, which thou lettest down into thy kəśad ; and when thou tələḥəq , so too it tələḥəq .
14.13: And when thou diest, thou lettest it down into thy kəśad ; and when the gunəd  draweth it, thou bringest them
14.14: And thou drawest its ʾaʿəṣuq ; for all the sinners are seized within it, as the cord is in their kəśawəd .
14.15: And He will bring all the souls of the sinners from where they were, from the ends of heaven; and likewise thy cord shall draw thee, that thou mayest bring thy soul from where thou wast, and thou shalt enter into the fäläg  of Sheol.
14.16: And thy flesh, täʾatito  and wino  sevenfold — as the flesh of our father Adam — the dew of His mercy shall raise thee, of God; and thereafter thou shalt be judged according as thou hast done evil and sin, according as thou hast not believed.
14.17: And it shall not profit thee and thou errest in thy night, who dwellest in the grave in thy error, and sayest: "There is no resurrection of the dead" — that they may err from the commandment of God.
14.18: And who shall yäḫaḏəg  thee in ashes and earth, that he may raise thee, that he may judge thee according to thy deeds which thou hast done?
14.19: And then He shall come — whence thy spirit which is in the winds, and whence thy dust which is in the earth, and whence thy flame which is in the fire.
14.20: And whence the spirit of life which was breathed upon thee, in the ʿaṣäd  of darkness.
14.21: Which täʿaʿəwaq  but the souls of the righteous in Paradise with joy are yətəʿaṣəwa .
14.22: But thou, O Judahite and Samaritan and Pharisee and Sadducee — until the time of thy judgment, thou shalt tətə ʿaśər  in darkness.
14.23: And then thou shalt see how God shall judge thee according to thy deeds, because thou hast ʾasə ḥatäkä luboʾo .
14.24: And thou shalt say unto them: "The dead shall not live; let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die." And thou sayest in thy kal , while thou sittest upon the seat of Moses: "There is no resurrection of the dead."
14.25: And therefore thou hast erred, while thou knowest the book of the Law, and teachest the word of the books; and thou causest men to err from ḫaḏsäyäkä , whereas thou hast not learned and dost not know.
14.26: The word of the books — thou exaltest the people of God with the evil of thy teaching, and with thy word which profiteth not.
14.27: But thou shalt be requited according to thy deeds, and according to the fruit of thy kännafr ; for God is no respecter of persons. And to those who learn good, He will reward them with good things, which He hath prepared for those who love Him.
14.28: But thou, thou hast nowhere to escape from His hand, who shall judge thee; and behold, He shall judge thee according to thy deeds. For thou and those whom thou hast mäharək-ed shall be judged.
14.29: I have told you that the dead shall rise. Then those who kept His commandment shall rise; and none shall yətəhakäl  to stand. For His commandment shall bring them forth — as the earth bringeth forth grass when the rain yəzäbəṭ .
14.30: And as the moist tree bringeth forth its shoot when the rain watereth the earth, and as it bringeth forth fruit — its root or the ear of grain — and it cannot withhold its fruit in the year God hath śämər-ed
14.31: And as conception, when ḥəmam  cometh, the womb cannot restrain it but when it heareth the voice of God, it beareth them for the dew which is from God shall come down upon it.
14.32: And likewise the earth shall bring forth it cannot restrain but when it heareth the voice of God, it beareth them for the dew which is from God shall come down upon it.
14.33: And the bodies shall be gathered into their places, where their ʾabədənət  fell; and one house of the treasuries of souls shall remain. And the souls shall enter into the bodies, from whence they went forth before.
14.34: And at the blowing of the horn, the dead shall rise in the twinkling of an eye; and they shall stand before God, and He shall requite them according to the work of their hands.
14.35: Then thou shalt see that thou shalt rise from the dead; and thou shalt be tanəkər-ed in all thy deeds which thou didst upon earth. And when thou seest them written before thine eyes — and this ʾamirä  thou shalt tənäsəḥ  — where it shall not profit thee.
14.36: And thou shalt know that thou shalt rise from the dead; and thou shalt be judged according to thy deeds which thou hast done.

15.1: But those who heard in their good deeds — then they shall rejoice. But those who täḥäkäyu , while they say "The dead shall not rise" — then they shall grieve, when they see that they are risen from the dead, with their evil deeds, which profit not.
15.2: And their deeds which they did shall judge them, while there is none to yəwäqəs  them They knew themselves how they shall be judged.
15.3: And they shall stand at the station of the wicked, in the day of weeping and of judgment, in the day of däyən , and in the day of God.
15.4: In the day of darkness, in the day of ṭaqa , in the day of gimi , in the day of ṣäʿəʿ , in the day of lightning.
15.5: In the day of fear and trembling, in the day of dädək  and märəqi , in the day of ʾasäḥatəya .
15.6: In the day the evil shall be requited according as he did evil; and in the day the pure shall be requited according as he did purity; and in the day the ṣəwag  shall be requited according as he did ṣug .
15.7: And in the day the master shall not be honoured above the servant, nor the maid above her mistress.
15.8: And in the day the king shall not be honoured above the poor, nor the ruler above the child, nor the father above his son, nor the mother above her daughter.
15.9: And in the day the baʿəl  shall not be honoured above the näday , nor the proud above the humble, nor the great above the small; for it is the day of justice, and the day of requital and of judgment — the day wherein He shall requite all according as he did.
15.10: And the day wherein the doers of good shall be rewarded; and in the day the evil, who did evil, shall be requited.
15.11: And the day, when they shall rejoice who were rewarded with good; and the day, when they shall grieve who were rewarded with evil. And they shall see those who ʾaḥäsäyu  the books, while they say: "The dead shall not rise."
15.12: Then shall all the sinners of the earth weep for their sins which they did; for there found them a sorrow which hath no comfort, because they did not good upon earth.
15.13: And likewise for the chosen also who did good, their joy shall not fail for ever and ever; for while they were upon earth, they hearkened to good deeds.
15.14: And they transgressed not the commandment of their Creator; for they knew that they should rise from the dead.
15.15: And because they transgressed not His commandment, they shall inherit
15.16: And in the heavens He hath given them to inherit the land of life, which He sware unto their fathers, in the day of resurrection, in the day yənädəyu * ʾabəʿəlt .*
15.17: And they shall yäʾawəyaw  — the doers of evil, who believe not the resurrection of the dead, nor the law of God; and the day of resurrection they remembered not.
15.18: Then they shall see thou shalt find them evil, which hath no maḫələqət , and which hath no healing therein, and no nuzaʾze ; and in their hearts a sorrow which hath no comfort, and no rest.
15.19: And ʿəṣe  which dieth not, and fire which is not quenched.
15.20: And upon their flesh: fire and täy , and a whirlwind, and ḥasätəya , and hail, and dädək  which yəzonəm  upon them.
15.21: Mäqaṣəḥ of fire for those who believe not the resurrection of the dead.

16.1: According to his work, and according to the cleanness of his hands.
16.2: And from whence cometh it that thou sayest: "These ṣəfər  of thy hands and thy feet, and the ṣägur  of thy head"? Did not God make them, that they should yəṣaʿ  — that thou mayest know the resurrection of the dead which shall be not in another flesh — that thou mayest know for thyself that thou shalt rise from the dead.
16.3: And thou shalt be judged according to thy deeds which thou hast done — evil and sin — at the resurrection of the dead; because thou hast caused the people to err, while thou sayest: "There is no resurrection of the dead."
16.4: And now thou shalt see, when the day of thy requital cometh unto thee; for what thou hast sown shall not ʾäʿabi  that it should profit — whence grain and whence root.
16.5: And again, thou who hast planted a tree — it shall not ʾäʿabu  Whence the vine, and whence the fig tree? Its shoot and its fruit shall not be changed.
16.6: And if thou hast planted a vine, it shall not be changed to become a fig tree; and if thou hast planted a fig, it shall not be changed to become a vine; and if thou hast sown a root, it shall not be changed to become sägäm .
16.7: And if thou hast sown sägäm , it shall not be changed to become a root. All these — in his seed and in his bäzämädu  and in his fruit and in his tree and in his bäqʷäṣəl  and in his bämərəw  — he shall receive blessing by the dew of mercy which is from God, and shall bring forth fruit.
16.8: Likewise the earth shall bring forth that which God hath sown; it shall profit soul and flesh — the doers of good, while they are not changed into doers of evil; and the doers of evil, while he is not changed into a doer of good. Those whom God hath sown shall profit in soul and flesh.
16.9: And when the time cometh for the blowing of the horn, the dead shall rise by the dew of mercy which is from God — who did good — in the resurrection of life; and their ʿəśet  — Paradise of joy — a dwelling for the pure, which He hath prepared for the chosen, where there is no disease and no sickness, where they shall not die again.
16.10: But those who did evil — in the resurrection of judgment — with the devil who ʾaləḥat  them.
16.11: And his evil angels who desire not to be saved, from all the servants of the living — in the judgment which is for ever.
16.12: Underneath, beneath, in the ṣənaf  of darkness, where is weeping and ḥaqəyäsənän , where there is no forgiveness and no mercy, and where there is no escape for ever and ever — because they did not good in their life upon earth, while they were in their flesh.
16.13: And therefore they shall be judged at the resurrection of soul and flesh.
16.14: For lelomu  — for those who believe not the resurrection of soul and flesh — with thee thus God shall show great is His täʾaməri .

17.1: And the grain of wheat: if it dieth not, it profiteth not and beareth no fruit; but if it dieth, the grain of wheat maketh root in the earth, and bringeth forth a shoot, and becometh an ear, and beareth fruit; and täʾaməru .
17.2: For you, that there may be many grains — one grain of wheat.
17.3: And likewise this grain profiteth from wind and water and earth; and the sun fire. For that which is without the sun cannot bear fruit
17.4: And the wind həyənt nädəs ; and that which is without wind cannot bear fruit And the water which yaśäqəya  and watereth the earth.
17.5: And when it is watered, dust and earth, it maketh root and yətəliḥal  upward, and beareth fruit by the ʾaməṭan  of the blessing of God.
17.6: For the grain of wheat is in the likeness of Adam, upon whom was breathed the spirit of God and the vine. Likewise it yəśäqəy  with water, and maketh root, and lifteth water the cord of fine root.
17.7: And it ascendeth heavenward, in the kätämä  of the shoot for the dew of mercy which is from God yaṭəbəw  them in the kätämä * ʾaḥərug  näwaḫatäwəyəbäsəl  by the flame of the sun; and it bringeth forth fruit which is from God.*
17.8: And it maketh a sweet savour which maketh glad the heart; and in it, when they eat it, it satisfieth as water; and bread — it shall not hunger nor thirst. And when yäʿaṣərəwa , it maketh dämä ʾaskal .
17.9: And when they drink it, it maketh glad the heart of man, as it saith in the Psalm: "Wine maketh glad the heart of man." And with śəmur  it intoxicateth when yabäqəʿ  his mouth and he yəwəḫaṭ  and yəmələʿ  in his sänəbəʿ ; and his blood yətəkäʿaw  in his heart.
17.10: And it yəresəy  him that is without heart; for the drunkenness of wine causeth to err exceedingly. And it yəresəy  him to ṣädəf  and to gʷäṣagʷäṣ  as the broad earth; and he knoweth not ʿəqəfət , nor the śok  that is in his hands and his feet.
17.11: And thus God made with the vine and its fruit, that His name may be yətəʾakʷat  — for those who do His will, and for those who believe the resurrection of the dead.
17.12: And He shall make them rejoice in the dwelling of life — for those who believe the resurrection of the dead.

18.1: From what error do ye err, O ye who believe not the resurrection of the dead? And when they lead you whither ye know not at this time tənəśəḥu  where it shall not profit you; and when they cast you into judgment, because ye believed not the resurrection of the dead, in flesh and soul ḫəburä .
18.2: And ye shall be requited according to your deeds, whether good or whether evil; for ye have ʾaḥəsäm-ed the heart of your kaləʾan , while ye say: "We believe that the dead shall not rise — who became ashes and earth."
18.3: And therefore their neighbours err; for there is no saḥət  for their death, and they cannot məqəś * fətomu  for they shall stand before the judge of God.*
18.4: And they shall be təḫaḏfəru-ed exceedingly, when He yəgeśəṣ  them in His wrath, and He shall yətəmäʿaʿ  them for all the evil which they did. For while they knew not the ways of God, they speak for ləlihomu  they knew not whence they came.
18.5: And they knew not whither they go, into the judgment of the burning fire. For according to the ṭəwəyät  of their heart they teach their neighbours; for bitter are they, and gʷäṣagʷäṣ  in their deeds, and ṣäwagan  and those who teach ṭəway * nägär , while they say: "There is no resurrection of the dead."*
18.6: And this ʾamirä  — they knew that the dead shall rise; and they shall be judged, because they believed not the resurrection of the dead — for all the creatures, the servants of the living.
18.7: For we are all the fruit of Adam, and through Adam we die; for for us all, through the sin of our father Adam, there found us the judgment of death from God.
18.8: And again, as we shall be judged according to what we have done, we shall rise with him, Adam our father; for through our father Adam's not knowing, täqänəy  entered the world unto death.
18.9: And therefore we are judged by the transgression of Adam; and our flesh is consumed in the grave, and our bones are täqäṭəqäṭu .
18.10: And the earth sätäyətät  our ʾanəgʷaʿ  and our masän  and our laḥəy  is consumed in ashes; and our flesh is tädäfənä  in the earth, and our good qal  is tädäfənä  in the earth.
18.11: And there went forth ʿəd  from our ʾayənt  shining and our masän  in the mäkab ; and it became dust.
18.12: Where is the beauty of their laḥəy  for the good wärazut  whom Adam qomomu  and śaʿəśaʿ  the taste of their words? Where is their greatness for the ṣənəʿan ?
18.13: And where is their strength for kings, and their honour for rulers? And they were täräsəyo  with horses, and täśärəgəwo  with gold and silver, and täräśəyo  with the goods of the field which yanəṣäbärəq .
18.14: Where is the taste of mäbaləʿət  in sweet wine?

19.1: O earth, that hast gathered kings and rulers, and the great and the honoured, and beautiful women, and fair virgins.
19.2: And strong hands, in whom was beauty, and fair  ʾaqʷayaṣ ; and in whom was knowledge and ləbuna ; and in whom was a fair voice, like the voice of ʾarəganon näbabit , and like the zəbəṭät  of the harp and ʿənəzira .
19.3: And in whom was fair song, who make rejoice as the drinking of wine, O son of Adam their eyes [were] shining like the morning stars.
19.4: And their yəman  was strong as he who yəhub  and he yənäśəʾ  and yäḥayəṣ  and their feet [were] fair to behold; and for those who yərəwəṣa  like mäkʷərakʷər * rətuʿat .*
19.5: I know thee, O Death, who hast taken their souls — of the fair hands; for by the will of the Lord God thou art täfänäwəkä .
19.6: But thou, O earth — for thou hast gathered many bodies, whom God brought forth from thee, and He shall bring them in unto thee. From thee we went forth, and unto thee we shall enter. By the will of God we täfäśaḥənä ; by the will of God, upon thee.
19.7: And thou art mändäf  for our limbs; we ʾansosäw  upon thee, and we nom  in thy wətit . We have eaten thy fruit, and thou hast eaten our flesh.
19.8: We have drunk from the dew of thy näqəʿ , and thou hast drunk from the näqəʿ  of our blood. We have eaten from the ʾanəgʷaʿ  of thy earth, and thou hast eaten from the ʾanəgʷaʿ  of our bones.
19.9: We have eaten from the taste of ashes; thy dew is fair, as God commanded thee, for our sisit . And thou hast taken the laḥəy  of our flesh, and thou hast räsäyəki-ed dust, as God commanded thee, for thy sisit .
19.10: O Death, from thee who hast gathered many of us — our mighty ones, kings and rulers — and thou fearedst not their gərəma  nor their greatness, as He commanded thee who created them; and thou ʾimänänəkä  the poor.
19.11: And thou ʾeməḥərəkä  those whose laḥəy  is fair; and thou sparedst not the mighty and the strong; and thou sparedst not the ʾabəʿəlt  and the nədayyan , the ḫaśuman  and the fair ʾaʿərug, and children of ʿədəw, and women.
19.12: And thou sparedst not those who think good and transgress not His commandment; and thou sparedst not those who think evil — who became as beasts in their deeds — nor those who are perfect in the beauty of their laḥəy , and their words, and the taste of their nägär .
19.13: And thou sparedst not those whose words are bitter, and full of märəgäm  in their mouths; and thou hast gathered their souls into thy treasuries — whether of light or whether of darkness.
19.14: And the earth hath gathered their flesh — whether in the kʷäkʷəḥ  or whether in the earth — until the blowing of the horn, when the dead shall rise.
19.15: And the doers shall be judged even according to their deeds which they did; for at the blowing of the horn and at the commandment of God the dead shall rise, in the twinkling of an eye; and they shall rejoice who did good.

20.1: Believe me, that He will spare none and will hide none — [even] all our deeds which we did upon the earth — when we stand before Him in fear and trembling.
20.2: And when we shall be filled with shame for our way, and when we have no garment for our nakedness.
20.3: And when we have no mərəguz  for our hands, nor ʿaśaʿ  for our feet.
20.4: And I know not his way, whither they shall lead us — whether däḫəṣ́ , or gwäṣ́agwəṣ́ , or darkness, or śok ; and moreover, whether the qälay  of the sea or the qälay  of Sheol.
20.5: And those who shall lead us, we shall not know them, and we shall not hear their speech.
20.6: And we shall not see their faces, for they are darkness; and in darkness they shall lead us.
20.7: As said David the prophet: When my soul was troubled within me — Thou, O Lord, didst shew my way. In this way I went; I hid my testimony; and I turned aside from the path of my right [hand]; and I saw, and I sinned against him who warned me; and in him I have no ʾämäśəṭ .
20.8: And this he saith: for he warneth that the demons yəśaläqəwo  him, and lead him unto him that knoweth not the way; and he turneth aside to the right and to the left; and there is none to find him who would make known.
20.9: And for me there is none to make known, but only in the midst of the angels of darkness.
20.10: And the spiritual angels of light, who are sent unto the ḫeran , that they may convey their souls unto the righteous, and lead them unto the ʿaṣ́äd  of the light of life.
20.11: And those — the angels of darkness and the demons — are sent unto the souls of sinners, that they may receive them and lead them away into the eternal judgment which is prepared for them, that they may be judged according to their deeds which they did.
20.12: Woe unto them, the souls of sinners, who are led into ḫagwəl ; and there is no rest, and no ʾädəḫin , and they shall not ʾäməśəṭ , and they shall not escape, for ever, from the tribulation which hath found them.
20.13: Woe unto them, the sinners! For in the way of Cain they went, and by the counsel of his error they täḫagulu-ed unto Balaam; and the sins which they commit; for bänäśiʾo * hələyanə  they went down, they yəmäkänəyu , that they might take others' goods by violence, which were not their goods.*
20.14: They indeed shall be judged according to their deeds which they did, in the judgment of burning fire.

21.1: Where are they that gathered up others' goods by violence, which were not their goods, and the work of their hands?
21.2: But — for they take others' goods, which are without śiṭ , and gather them up — while they know not the day of their death. Thou shalt overtake them, and they shall leave to another their bəʿəl .
21.3: And their children shall not rejoice in the bəʿəl  of their fathers; for they are houses of sinners — whether yamänäzəzəwomu , or by theft, or by təʿəgələy ; those like them are sinners, like their fathers; or by ḥäyəd .
21.4: And there is none to preserve for them the goods of their fathers; for in violence they gathered them for themselves. And like the śaḥəw  of a cloud, and like smoke which the wind lifteth, and like the fruit of grass which is shaken, and like wax which melteth before the face of fire — so shall perish the glory of the sinners.
21.5: As said David: I saw the wicked great and exalted, like the cedar of Lebanon; and when I returned, I ḫaṭaʾəkəwo-ed; I sought him, and found not his place.
21.6: And likewise is the destruction of the sinners, in məʿər : that they shall not be established, those who oppress their neighbours — though they are not as those who die not — because they gathered others' goods by ʿa mäṣ́a .
21.7: O servants, remember that ye shall pass away, and your bəʿəl  also shall pass away with you; and though [it be] with much of your silver, and your gold also, there shall be that which is left.
21.8: And if ye multiply children, there shall be many graves; and if ye multiply houses, there shall be mäzəbär .
21.9: And if ye multiply cattle, they shall be a spoil to your enemies; for ye have not done the will of the Lord God your God. And all that your hands have produced shall not be found, for it is not blessed.
21.10: Whether of the house or of the field; whether with ʾäʿəʿod  and fruit, or with ḥätəl ; or with the produce of ʿəkəl  and məkəyad  and wine.
21.11: And if ye rejoice not in the fruit of your wombs, but sorrow shall be unto you from all your enemies; for God shall not prosper you with all the men of your house; for ye have not kept the commandments of the Lord God.
21.12: But unto those who keep His law and His commandment and His statute, He shall not withhold them from His blessing; and He shall give them all that they ask; and He shall bless for them the fruit of their land and the fruit of their wombs.
21.13: And He shall cause them to inherit the exaltation above all the nations which ʿawədu  them, that they may be [exalted?], and not that they be brought low; and He shall give them all blessing, in their increase and their fruit.
21.14: And all which their hands have produced, He shall bless for them the fruit of their tillage, and the increase of their cattle; and He shall make them rejoice in the fruit of their wombs.
21.15: And He shall multiply for them their cattle, and save them from all their tribulations, from disease and dəkam , and from the mänəsut  of those who know and of those who know not.
21.16: And He shall stand for them in the midst of judgment, and save them from tribulation and from evil speech and from all that riseth up; for at the first he made the tabernacle. If a Levite, who is blameless and strong, keepeth the service of the tabernacle and walketh in the will of the Lord God — by the former law he [the Israelite] shall give him the tithe of all that cometh in, and every firstborn from man even unto cattle.
21.17: And a city of refuge in all their lands, as Moses commanded Joshua the son of Nun, that the slayer might be saved who slew unwittingly — or whether wittingly.
21.18: Until they bring him unto judgment, to condemn him or to justify him.
21.19: And by your inquiry they shall say unto them: "If there was hatred with him—" And he shall say: "For unwittingly there fell from my hand an axe, or a stone, or a tree, and he died, he upon whom it fell." Know ye: save him, for unwittingly he did it; he shall be saved.
21.20: But as for him who did it wittingly, he shall be judged according to his sin, and there is none to pity him. But as for him who did it unwittingly — though he killed — by your inquiry, spare him, that he die not; for unwittingly he did it.
21.21: And thus Moses commanded the children of Israel, that they should not transgress the commandment of the Lord God, but that they should keep themselves from all evil — he commanded them.
21.22: And he commanded them also, that they should walk in all His judgments; and the righteous shall fädəfad  put far from themselves ʾägəʿ  and bətək  and death, and from all that is unseemly for the children of men — that those who walk in the commandment of the Lord God may do them, and those who cease from all evil, as he commanded them.
21.23: And he commanded them, that they should not transgress the commandment which he ordained for them, according to the pattern which came  mayat  — which is the tabernacle — that their souls might be saved, and they might find their rest with their fathers who did good.
21.24: For those who believed in the word of the Lord God, and walked in the commandment — they shall be called təwə lədä  of the righteous; for from Adam and Seth are they, who did the will of the Lord God — we ʾiyəmenənə .
21.25: For we are the seed of Adam; and in His likeness we were läḥäkwänä ; and in His image He created us, that a goodly dawn might shine; and all who keep unto the Lord God.
21.26: And as for us, we have done good; we shall inherit the land of the living with those who did good — for there is no destruction and no night — for those who love Him.
21.27: And fädəfad  He shall love them, and hear their prayer — for those who call upon Him in purity — and He shall yətəwe * käfə  their nəsəḥ  — for those who are pure in ṭəbuʿ  — and He shall give them might and ṣ́änəʿ , to those who keep His law and His statute and His commandment.*
21.28: And they shall rejoice with Him in the kingdom which is for ever — those who did His will — whether first or last; unto Him they shall offer the sacrifice of praise, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
